message.content:
I bought AAPL. Here's the summary.

**What I did and why.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and checked the live quote ($222.70 last / $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask at 15:05 UTC on 2024-11-06), then placed a single buy limit order for **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75**, which filled at $222.75 for about **$9,801** — within the $10,000 per-order cap, the only order placed today so the $20,000 daily cap is far from binding, and well under the $50,000 cash balance, so no money left the account. The bull case in the filing is that revenue was **$391,035 million** (up 2% year over year, driven by Services up 13% to $96,169 million), gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, and **operating income rose to $123,216 million** from $114,301 million. **Net income of $93,736 million** and **diluted EPS of $6.08** were down slightly only because of a one-time, non-operating $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision — a purge that doesn't touch the operating engine — while **operating cash flow of $118,254 million** funded $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends. The offsetting negatives I weighed are real: iPhone sales were flat at $201,183 million, Greater China fell 8%, and at $222.70 the stock trades around 36–37× trailing diluted EPS, so this is a quality-at-a-full-price purchase rather than a bargain — which is why I sized it as one modest tranche of about 20% of available cash instead of a full $10,000-plus commitment. One data caveat worth recording: the filing's "Highlights" line and statement-of-operations line report FY2024 total net sales as $94,930 million, but that is internally inconsistent with the product, segment, and cost-of-sales tables (which sum to $391,035 million); I relied on $391,035 million as the correctly reported revenue.
